text.en:
Mina hung wet clothes in the sun. After some time they were dry.
"Where did the water go?" she asked.
Her grandmother said, "It went into the air as vapour. One day it will come back as rain."

Water on the ground, in rivers, lakes and seas is heated by the Sun and changes into water vapour. This is evaporation.
Water vapour rises, cools in the sky and changes into tiny drops that form clouds. This is condensation.
When the drops in clouds become heavy, they fall as rain, snow or hail. This is precipitation. The water flows into rivers and the sea, and the cycle goes on and on.
The Sun heats water and it rises as water vapour. This is evaporation.
High up, the vapour cools and turns into tiny drops that make clouds. This is condensation.
When the drops become heavy they fall as rain. Rivers carry the water to the sea.
Then the cycle starts again. This is the water cycle.

problem.en: Put these in order: rain falls, water evaporates, clouds form.

text.en: First the Sun heats water and it evaporates.
Then the vapour cools and forms clouds.
Finally the clouds give rain. So: evaporate, clouds form, rain falls.

prompt.en: A friend asks where rain water comes from. Explain in two lines.

requiredIdeas.en: Water from seas and rivers evaporates and rises.
It cools into clouds and falls back as rain.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking rain is made in the clouds from nothing.

points.en: Condensation turns vapour into drops and clouds.
Rain brings water back, and the cycle repeats.
